samehost matches the server's own IP addresses, and samenet matches addresses in directly connected subnets. When a host name is used, PostgreSQL first checks reverse resolution of the client IP to a host name, then does a forward lookup of that host name to confirm the client address.

peer is only for local connections (Unix-domain sockets) and obtains the OS user name from the kernel, while ident is only for TCP/IP connections and uses the IDENT protocol (RFC 1413) via an external service on port 113; if ident is specified for a local connection, PostgreSQL uses peer instead.

PostgreSQL supports RANGE, LIST, and HASH partitioning on a partitioned table. RANGE and LIST partitioning benefit most from partition pruning, allowing the query planner to skip scanning partitions that cannot contain matching rows when the WHERE clause contains a constant expression on the partition key; HASH partitioning does not benefit from pruning because each row maps to a fixed bucket regardless of query pattern.
The table must have a constraint that exactly matches the partition boundary.

A role with LOGIN can be used to log in (a user), while a role without LOGIN cannot log in directly (a group); roles without LOGIN are commonly used as groups to which LOGIN roles are granted membership via GRANT.
SET ROLE changes current_user to the specified role if the current user is a member of it, while session_user remains the original login role.

pg_basebackup creates a binary copy of the entire running database cluster and works with the streaming replication protocol to take a consistent snapshot without blocking writes, making it the foundation for setting up a new standby server and suitable for full cluster backups. pg_dump produces a logical backup of a single database as a SQL script or custom-format archive, is online (does not block reads or writes), and is the standard tool for migrations and small-to-medium backups.
log_min_duration_statement logs any SQL statement that runs for at least the specified number of milliseconds; setting it to 0 logs every statement, producing high volume.
